items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VIII, List of Answers on Topics 80:1
items.html: The source of the division within Bina is in the ten Sefirot of direct light. For there we find two degrees within Bina of direct light, since her GAR are on her back toward Hochma, in the secret of “for she desires Hesed,” and she desires only the Hassadim she receives from Keter, as is known. However, at the time she emanates the ZAT of direct light — and it is known that the ZAT of direct light are not emanated except in an illumination of Hochma, for this is the whole distinction between ZA and Bina, that Bina is entirely Hassadim, without Hochma, whereas ZA, though its own essence too is Hassadim, nonetheless has within it also an illumination of Hochma (as stated in Part One, page 5, Sub Header, “And the Reason”).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VIII, List of Answers on Topics 80:2
items.html: Hence, when Bina emanates to ZON, she is compelled to break off her back that faced Hochma, and to turn her face to Hochma, in order to receive from it an illumination of Hochma for the sake of ZA. And then, within Bina herself too, ZAT expand, since the ZAT of Bina are the root of ZON of direct light, which remain within Bina, since there is no absence in the spiritual, and hence the root of the lower always remains within the upper, as is known. Behold, before you: the GAR of Bina of direct light are entirely Hassadim alone, with their back toward Hochma; but her ZAT are already in an illumination of Hochma. These are the two degrees that came to be within Bina, and not within the rest of the Sefirot of direct light. Hence the level of Bina of Atzilut, too, divides into two degrees: into the aspect of Aba ve Ima Ilain, who are the aspects of GAR of Bina and are the aspect of Hassadim alone, and into the aspects of YESHSUT, who are in an illumination of Hochma. But the rest of the Sefirot each took a whole level: for Atik took the level of Keter, AA took the level of Hochma, and ZA took the level of ZA, together with which Malchut also came.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VIII, List of Answers on Topics 80:3
items.html: And there is a second reason, which likewise follows from the reason above, which is that all twelve Partzufim of Atzilut are considered a single Partzuf, as is known. And in this general sense, there are found two aspects that divide at the chest, since so it is with every individual Partzuf: from the chest upward there is the screen of the Yesod of Ima, and hence the Hassadim are covered and there is no revelation of an illumination of Hochma there, whereas from the chest downward the Hassadim are revealed in an illumination of Hochma, as is known. And so it is also at the chest of AA of Atzilut, for up to the chest the Yesod of Atik rules, which is the aspect of the root for Hassadim, as above in Answer 130. Hence up to there, Aba ve Ima Ilain expand, which are the aspect of GAR of the level of Bina of MA, since they nurse from the Yesod of Atik. And from the chest downward, YESHSUT are revealed in an illumination of Hochma, since the rule of the Yesod of Atik has already ceased there, they are able to receive an illumination of Hochma from AA. Behold, that the screen of the Yesod of Atik at the place of the chest of AA is the cause that Aba ve Ima and YESHSUT became two degrees, whereby Aba ve Ima Ilain are compelled to receive from the Yesod of Atik, and YESHSUT are compelled to receive from AA, once the Yesod of Atik has ceased. And if you divide the whole of Atzilut by Guf and Etzem, and AHP, you will find that the place of the cut between them is exactly at the place of the chest. For Atik is the secret of Galgalta, meaning Keter of MA, and AA is the secret of Einayim, meaning Hochma of MA, and Aba ve Ima Ilain are the aspect of GAR of Bina, to whom the matter of going outward does not apply, and their end is at the chest, as above. And from the chest downward are found the ZAT of the ear, which are YESHSUT, and ZON, which are Hotem, Peh. (Inner Observation, item 11, and Inner Light, page 666, Sub Header, “And With This”)
